texts: Ebstein's anomaly includes a thin-walled atrialized component of the right ventricle: C.
The septal and posterior leaflets are displaced toward the apex, so the inlet portion above them works as part of the atrium although it is ventricle in origin, often thin and dilated.
The anterior leaflet stays attached at the annulus, large and sail-like, with abnormal attachments to the ventricular wall below.
The functional right ventricle is made of the trabecular (apical) and outlet portions, and the outlet is preserved, not small or absent.
In the picture, above Einstein's pushed-down prongs, the top of the blue engine room has become a paper-thin extra lobby.
Memory hook: Einstein pushes the prongs down, and the room above turns into lobby.
